- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to underreact to bullish events — adjust forecast upward by 1–2% relative to recent high.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overcorrects downward — reduce forecast slope by 0.5–1.5% per day to avoid overshoot.
- If official event net supply is negative and bearish sentiment dominates (≥0.67), model underestimates downside risk — add 0.5–1.5% downward bias to forecast.
- When multiple consecutive auctions occur (≥3 in 30d), model tends to overestimate price stability — introduce slight downward drift (0.1–0.3% per day) to reflect supply pressure.
- If sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.33–0.67), model often fails to capture mean reversion — apply slight upward bias (0.2–0.5%) to avoid underestimating volatility.
- For 30d forecasts, if true outcome deviates >3% from 14d moving average, adjust forecast to align with recent 7d trend — avoid long-term drift unless sentiment confirms trend.
